text:
maria: heads-up — Amy on Dedicated reported a sudden surge of 401s right after rotating their API key in Vault. They applied a k8s secret update and did a rolling restart, but errors continued for about 10 minutes.

bob: do we know which redwood-python version they're running? any logs or a minimal repro?

maria: Amy pasted repro steps: deploy a daemonset whose app creates the Redwood client at module import time; rotate secret in Vault and update the k8s secret via envFrom: secretRef; pods restart but their long-running worker process keeps returning 401s until the process is fully restarted.

customer-amy: exact minimal snippet they shared:
```python
# main.py
import os
from redwood import RedwoodClient

API_KEY = os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')  # captured at import
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=API_KEY)

def handle(req):
    return client.generate(req)
```

maria: container runs with gunicorn using UvicornWorker and uses preload behavior. That means module imports are evaluated before workers fork. When the secret changed on the node, the process retained the old env value.

alex: yes — two causes: module-level client + preloaded/forking server. k8s env updates (via secretRef) only affect container env on start; they don't magically update running process env.

bob: did they mount as a file projection previously? they said envFrom, so new values only on container start. If gunicorn preloads or forks before the new env is set, children can inherit stale values.

alex: mitigation suggestions we recommended to Amy: keep client creation lazy (read env at runtime), or ensure workers are restarted so processes re-read env. For gunicorn: disable --preload or use graceful full worker restarts. On k8s: prefer kubectl rollout restart to ensure new pods pick up updated env vars.

alex: example lazy init pattern we suggested:
```python
_client = None

def get_client():
    global _client
    if _client is None:
        _client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
    return _client
```

maria: customer switched to lazy init and performed a full restart of the pods; 401s stopped. They also upgraded redwood-python from 0.4.1 to 0.4.2 — the newer release raises a clearer error when api_key is None which helped them debug faster.

bob: action items
- eng: add a short doc/FAQ entry "SDK init and env propagation" covering gunicorn preload and k8s secret updates
- devex: update our starter templates to avoid module-level client creation (I found one example that does this)
- support: send KB to Amy summarizing the root cause and workaround patterns

alex: I will open a PR to change the template to lazy init and add a note in README, tagging infra for review.

sre-bot: incident-note INC-2026-042 created — root cause: module-level RedwoodClient + preloaded process prevented env rotation from taking effect. Mitigation: restart processes; update docs/templates.

maria: Amy confirmed the mitigation worked and will monitor. We'll close the escalation once the PR merges. Thanks everyone :sparkles:
